Merely because offence involves a minor and the occurrence is of heinous offence, it did not absolve the prosecution of its responsibility to conduct itself with all sincerity-to adduce and collect hard evidence and to prove it, to establish that the appellant had caused the occurrence.
Reasonable doubt exists that the occurrence was caused otherwise than narrated by the prosecution.
The chain of evidence is broken in vital parts.
It is not clear that the deceased was last seen with the appellant soon before her disappearance.
It is also not clear from the evidence that he had fled from the spot.
Rather it is proven, he had joined the search for her, with P.W.1.
No corroborative material exists to establish that either rape or murder or both were committed by the appellant.
